issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) refers to a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but both the template Main and the provided solution implement and call a method named computeMealCost(Meal) instead. This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the code will confuse students about which method to implement and may cause compilation/test failures if they follow the spec but the template/solution expect the other name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the method in the solution and template to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (keeping it static and returning int), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to require computeMealCost(Meal): int. Also update example calls in Main to use the chosen name so students and tests are unambiguous.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML expect a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute the net cost of a meal, but the implementation uses a differently named method (computeMealCost). Additionally, example usages across repositories are inconsistent: the template Main calls computeMealCost, the solution SealSaloon defines computeMealCost, while the solution Main calls calculateTotalPrice. This inconsistent naming for the single conceptual operation (compute total price of a Meal) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement (calculateTotalPrice) to available code and examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the operation across all artifacts. Either rename SealSaloon.computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice (and update any callers), or update the problem statement and example usages to refer to computeMealCost. Ensure Main, template comments, UML, and SealSaloon implementation all use the same identifier.
